subject: Re: DPA clarifications — controller/processor roles & breach notice
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T15:05:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap + DPA items we promised

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and the privacy items you asked us to confirm: 

1) Controller vs. Processor: Redwood operates as a processor for inference requests where you (Acme Payments) send customer data to our hosted service; you remain the data controller for your customers' personal data. We can confirm the DPA language will reflect that. Marissa (cc'd) is our privacy lead and will share the exact clause we propose.

2) Subprocessors: We listed our standard subprocessors in the DPA appendix. You asked about caching/KV engines and analytics — those are covered and we allow for customer review and objection with a 30-day cure period.

3) Breach notice timing: We commit to notify affected customers and Acme within 72 hours of becoming aware of a qualifying security incident per the DPA. We also provide post-incident reports and remediation steps.

4) Data residency & retention: For production inference, data is stored transiently for inference processing and cached for performance per configured retention policy. We support region-specific hosting (US/EU) for residency; retention windows are configurable and we will include options in the DPA.

Next steps:
- Marissa will send a short DPA clarification doc and attach the redline we discussed.
- If your legal team has remaining redlines, please send them to legal@redwood.com and we'll prioritize a response.
- Propose a follow-up call next Wednesday to walk through any outstanding redlines.

Thanks — Ben

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we loop legal:

- Can you confirm whether Redwood ever acts as a controller for any inference data (e.g., model improvement)? Our concern is about using customer PII to improve models.
- For subprocessors: is there a published list with contact for objections? We don't object to cloud infra providers but want visibility on any analytics or profiling vendors.
- Breach notice: 72 hours is reasonable. Do you provide initial acknowledgement + 30-day root-cause update as part of the standard DPA?
- Retention: you mentioned caching. If we set retention to 0 days for logs, does Redwood still keep any operational logs for debugging/traceability? If so, what is the retention and how is it protected?

Cc'ing Legal (legal@acme-payments.com) to start the review. Can Marissa or Rishi respond with the DPA language and SOC2 excerpt?

Hi Alex / Acme legal team — following up with the specific language and attachments you requested. Answers below and attached excerpts: SOC2-summary.txt (SOC 2 Type II scope) and a redline of our standard DPA (DPA_redline_v2.pdf).

Controller vs Processor: Redwood acts as a processor for customer-supplied data used for inference. We do not use customer-provided PII to train or improve public models unless explicitly agreed and documented in the DPA (opt-in). Our standard DPA contains a prohibition on using customer data for model improvement without written consent and an option for customers to opt in to a separate processing agreement if they want model-improvement benefits.

Subprocessors: We publish a current list of subprocessors at https://redwood.com/subprocessors and will notify customers 30 days ahead of any additions. Customers have 30 days to object; objections are escalated to our legal team for review and potential mitigation. If you need the contact for objections, please send a directed notice to legal@redwood.com and we will coordinate.

Breach notice: Our standard commitment is to provide initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware of a qualifying incident, followed by periodic updates and a root cause and remediation report within 30 days where feasible. We will include these timelines in the DPA redline.

Retention & operational logs: For inference calls, payloads are processed transiently. We retain request/response logs for debugging and telemetry; default retention is 30 days but can be configured down to 0 days upon request. Note: even with 0-day customer request-data retention, operational logs (meta logs, trace IDs, error stacks) may be retained for a limited period (default 90 days) to support availability and incident investigations; these logs are pseudonymized and access-controlled. We can include contractual commitments around log access, encryption-at-rest, and KMS-backed key management.

Next steps:
- See attached redline and SOC2 excerpt.
- Ben: can you put together a 30-minute follow-up with Acme legal to walk through any specific redlines?

Thanks — Marissa
